method: Independent visible normal-URL play, two fresh browser attempts to terminal screens. Read visible-playtest help first. No source, other reviews, hidden state, evaluation, test URL, privileged controller, or arrangements used.
overall: Atmospheric and coherent playable slice with satisfying critical-hit and memory-recovery feedback. Distinct cover routes and a multi-coil boss give the mission structure. My exposed, imprecise routing was punished strongly; this is not evidence of an impossible mission. Geometric actors, repeated architecture, small dense labels and incomplete tested mission coverage do not support AAA readiness.

controls.actuallyUsed: WASD, held-RMB relative look and aimed left-button rifle fire, R reload, hold E, M map, Shift dash, Space jump/vault, visible resume/deploy UI. Did not test crouch, sprint, weapon2 or Tab trace.
controls.aiming: Uncaptured turning required helper-held RMB. Approximately850 relative pixels yielded61 degrees under ADS. Small vertical adjustment -30 aligned induction optic for critical kill. Large turns required several valid drags. No continuous human aiming; captures normally released inputs and paused via Escape.

strengths: Rain, wet lighting and cyan/amber palette form a clear identity.
Map distinguishes walls and low cover, receiver destinations and uplink.
Objective changes, recovery cards and terminal results clearly communicate progress.
Boss coil percentages and disable announcement gave useful confirmation.
friction: Receiver direction marker can remain through large opaque surfaces; distance alone did not identify the reachable entrance until map and south-intake guidance were combined.
Small thin type on map/HUD requires attention amid layered announcements.
Enemies can keep pressuring during navigation; my attempts neglected most patrols, which materially contributed to both losses.
Blocky repeated robot models and simple environment geometry remain visibly prototype-like despite strong lighting.

limits: Paused synthetic input/capture with short batches; browser scheduling and screenshots interrupt natural pacing.
Limited continuous-human aiming and enjoyment assessment; scores reflect observed structure and feedback, not a claim of human feel.
Audio not audibly assessed; no judgement of mix, spatial cues or soundtrack quality.
Software-WebGL fallback reported; no hardware GPU performance, latency, framerate or stability certification.
No full upload, service, alternate weapon, crouch/sprint or successful terminal victory coverage.
